title: GeoJSON 3D Terrain Overlay
prompt:
Build procedurally generated noise heightmap terrain with Three.js, and overlay hardcoded GeoJSON polygon regions on top of it.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Strictly Followed)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Terrain]
(1) Procedurally generate a 128×128 heightmap using Perlin/Simplex-like noise, and render the grid as a lit Mesh.
(2) Use an elevation-based material with a low-to-high color gradient.

[GeoJSON]
(3) Hardcode a simple FeatureCollection containing exactly 5 Polygon regions, which may represent simplified national borders or administrative regions, with coordinates mapped to the terrain plane's extent.
(4) Project the polygons onto the terrain surface, either along the normals or by sampling terrain heights, and render them as semi-transparent colored overlay layers.
(5) When a region is clicked, highlight that region and display statistics such as approximate area and average elevation; a DOM panel with id="regionStats" may be used.

[Layer Toggles]
(6) id="terrainToggle": toggle the visibility of the terrain Mesh.
(7) id="regionToggle": toggle the visibility of the region overlay layers.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  terrainVertices: number,
  regionCount: number,
  selectedRegion: null | number | string,
  maxElevation: number,
  minElevation: number,
  layerVisibility: { terrain: boolean, regions: boolean }
}

Output a single HTML file that can be opened directly in a browser and run.
physics_constraints: Exactly 5 polygon regions from hardcoded GeoJSON
